result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as mock resources (test scope), whatever follows it. The new test passes (2 tests, 0 failures).

**Change** in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`, `addTestConventions`:
- `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` became `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*`
- `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` became `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`

The `[^/]*` matches any characters within a single folder name, including punctuation, non-ASCII, and an empty suffix (plain `mock/`). The leading `/` keeps `remock/` out, and the trailing `/` keeps files like `mock.java` and `mockery.java` out. `SourceFileFilter` already tries backslash variants of the path, so Windows paths are covered. The existing `mockapi`, `mocks`, `__mocks__`, `mock-data`, `mock_data`, `mock data` and `mockStore` cases still match.

**New test**: `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsMockTest.java`. It checks positive cases (the elasticsearch `mock/` path, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe`, `mock模拟`, the previously supported folders, and backslash paths) and negative cases (`remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java`, `mockery.java`).

Nothing is committed.
